translation:
Strengthens the master of water; when the left chi pulse is weak, tonify the water to match the fire.

Huai Dihuang (washed with wine, steamed and sun-dried nine times, then boiled in wine until soft and pounded into a paste, 8 liang), Huai Shanyao (4 liang, stir-fried), Shanzhuyu (core removed, 4 liang, washed, steamed, and stir-fried over a slow fire), Bai Fuling (skin and bits removed, cleanly steamed and sun-dried, 3 liang), Mudanpi (bone removed, 3 liang), Guang Zexie (fuzz removed, 3 liang).

Make all into powder, pound evenly together with the Dihuang paste, add refined honey, and make into pills the size of wuzi (Chinese parasol seeds). Each day on an empty stomach swallow three qian with boiling water, and immediately press it down with fine food. It reaches the kidney channel directly, and there is no matter of it sticking in the diaphragm.

Adding Danggui, Wuwei, Shengdihuang, and Chaihu makes it named the Yiyin Shenqi Pill. (Equal parts)

Add Gouqi and white chrysanthemum.
translator_notes: 左尺 (left chi) is the left-hand chi pulse, which reflects the yin of the kidneys.
梧子大 (wuzi size) means the size of Chinese parasol seeds.
懷地黃/懷山藥 (Huai Dihuang/Huai Shanyao) refer to Rehmannia and yam from Huaiqing.
光澤瀉 (Guang Zexie) means high-quality Alisma.
